samples.summary: backend.md — the canonical backend design doc — is left describing the old auth surface, so the repo now has two design docs that contradict each other on the same endpoints. The change updates cli.md and rest-api.md only, but backend.md's API Reference still documents `GET /auth/github` as plain "Initiates GitHub OAuth flow" with no `state`/cookie (line 103-105), `GET /auth/github/callback` as unconditionally upserting the user and setting cookies with no state validation (line 107-115), and `POST /auth/cli/exchange` as `Body: { code }` (line 146) with no `codeVerifier`. The cookie table (lines 312-313) lists only `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` and omits the new `wafflebase_oauth_state` (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, path=/auth, 5 min), and the Observability section's redaction bullet (line 348-349) lists only header redaction, not the new `/auth` query-string redaction the `req` serializer now performs. CONTRIBUTING's design-doc discipline expects the canonical subsystem doc to be folded forward with an architecture/behavior change of this size.
samples.evidence: backend.md:103-115 (`/auth/github`, callback), :146 (`Body: { code }`), :312-313 (cookie table), :348-349 (redaction) vs app.module.ts:70 `logSafeUrl`, github-auth.guard.ts (state cookie), auth.dto.ts `codeVerifier`.

samples.summary: The CLI now writes a new artifact into `~/.wafflebase/` (`login-url.txt`, 0600, transient), but cli.md's canonical "All CLI state lives under `~/.wafflebase/`" tree (lines 110-116) still lists only `config.yaml` and `session.json`. The new file is only mentioned in prose inside the login-flow narrative, so the one place a reader looks for "what does the CLI put on my disk" is incomplete — and this file holds live login secrets, which makes it the most important entry to list.
samples.evidence: cli.md:110-116 file tree unchanged; login.ts announceLoginUrl writes join(dirname(getConfigPath()), 'login-url.txt').

samples.summary: The guard applies the change's own stated principle ("missing or malformed is a 400 naming the parameter, never a login that quietly continues unbound") to `nonce` and `code_challenge` but not to `port`: a `mode=cli` request with an out-of-range or non-numeric `port` still falls through to `req.__oauthState = 'w.'+…` and completes as a *browser* login, setting session cookies in the browser and redirecting to FRONTEND_URL while the CLI sits until its 30-second timeout. rest-api.md's updated §7 describes `mode=cli` requests as validated (`port` must be 1024–65535) and never says a bad port silently becomes a web login, so the documented and implemented shapes diverge on the one CLI parameter that was not tightened.
samples.evidence: github-auth.guard.ts: port range check gates state creation; the following `if (!req.__oauthState)` block converts the request into a web login. docs/design/rest-api.md:331-360 describes required-parameter 400s for the CLI start URL.

samples.summary: With the guard now validating `port` (1024–65535) before any state entry is created, the controller's repeat range check on `cliState.port` is unreachable defence-in-depth; harmless, but it leaves two owners for the same rule and rest-api.md documents it only once.
samples.evidence: github-auth.guard.ts validates portNum before createState; auth.controller.ts re-checks `port < 1024 || port > 65535` on the consumed state.

samples.summary: `StateEntry.mode` / `CliStateParams.mode` is now vestigial: the only caller (`GitHubAuthGuard`) creates state exclusively when `mode === 'cli'`, and the browser flow uses the cookie double-submit rather than the store, so the field can only ever hold `'cli'` while the controller still branches on it. The store's own doc comment claims every field is a required binding, which `mode` is not.
samples.evidence: github-auth.guard.ts:121 createState({ mode, … }) inside `if (mode === 'cli' && port)`; auth.controller.ts:191 re-checks `state.mode === 'cli'`.

samples.summary: Scope: this PR bundles two unrelated workstreams — the OAuth loopback/PKCE/browser-CSRF hardening and the #661 CLI error-envelope `command` attribution refactor (which touches ~20 CLI files). The task doc records and justifies the shared branch, so this is noted rather than blocked, but it does make the diff hard to review as one change and means the envelope refactor lands without an issue of its own in scope here.

verdict.reason: Verified every quoted location. docs/design/backend.md still documents the pre-change auth surface: line 103-105 `GET /auth/github` with no state; 107-115 callback with no state validation; 144-147 `POST /auth/cli/exchange` `Body: { code }` with no codeVerifier; 310-313 cookie table without `wafflebase_oauth_state`; 348-349 redaction bullet listing only header/set-cookie redaction. A case-insensitive grep of backend.md for `state|verifier|redact|nonce` returns a single hit (line 349), and the file contains no link to rest-api.md/cli.md that would delegate the auth surface (its only doc links are yorkie-auth-webhook.md:135, document-copy.md:180, sharing.md:198). Meanwhile the code does implement the new behavior (github-auth.guard.ts:15 OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE, auth.dto.ts:16 codeVerifier, cli-auth.store.ts:120-134 PKCE check, app.module.ts:70 logSafeUrl), and it is documented only in rest-api.md:334-367,401 and cli.md. docs/design/README.md:153 still designates backend.md as the doc covering the backend "API reference, auth system", so the repo now carries two design docs contradicting each other on the same endpoints — the folding-forward discipline in CONTRIBUTING.md:57-61. No counterexample found anywhere in docs/design.

finding.summary: Scope: two unrelated efforts are bundled in one change. (a) OAuth security hardening — CLI nonce echo, PKCE S256, browser double-submit `state` cookie, `/auth` access-log redaction — touching backend auth guard/controller/store and cli login; and (b) the CLI error-envelope refactor attributed to #661 — one-line envelopes, `command` attribution, shared `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope`, session-command conversion — touching ~20 CLI files. Only the `login` failure-reporting rewrite sits at their intersection. No originating issue accompanied this review, so I cannot map either half to an acceptance criterion; if the charter is one of the two, the other half is unrequested scope.
finding.evidence: diff spans packages/backend/src/auth/* (PKCE/CSRF) and packages/cli/src/{commands,docs,notes,slides,files}/* (envelope attribution) with independent doc sections in rest-api.md and cli.md §9/§10

verdict.reason: The finding is conditional on its own premise: "if the charter is one of the two, the other half is unrequested scope." That premise is contradicted by the repository. Both halves are chartered work with their own plan-of-record and fully-checked acceptance criteria: docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md (Issue #661; criteria lines 56-63) and docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md (Related #654/#655, RFC 8252 §8.9, RFC 7636; criteria lines 113-133). docs/tasks/README.md:1-16 establishes these todo files as the repo's task plan/review record. The co-landing is not an unexplained bundle: 20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:24-30 explicitly records "**Where it landed.** It rides the #661 branch again (PR #786), not a separate one… the two touch `login.ts` from opposite ends (the OAuth handshake vs. the failure envelope), so splitting them now would mean two PRs whose only conflict is that file." Design-doc discipline is met for both halves in the canonical subsystem docs rather than parallel files (docs/design/cli.md:200-244 §3.1 loopback binding; docs/design/cli.md:1094-1147 §9/§10 envelope; docs/design/rest-api.md:334-402), so the "independent doc sections" the reviewer cites as evidence of creep are in fact the required folding-in. Neither half is unrequested, no stated Non-Goal is exceeded, and no acceptance criterion is unmet — the residue is a PR-hygiene preference about splitting branches, which this lens rates minor and never blocking. Note: the underlying code the reviewer describes IS present (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:58-161; packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:47-58,283-336; packages/backend/src/auth/cli-auth.store.ts:13-139); it is the scope-creep characterization, not the code, that is refuted.
